contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #297: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem.

The staged September 24 2026 selective bridge in OpenAI manuscript family 297, under faithful trace, no finite-dimensional irreducibles, and inequivalent equal-trace peaking projection states; all norm limits use the full product directed set.

definitions.admissible_pair: h=k, or inequivalent h,k not the designated pair of classes; inside a designated class choose its peaking representative
definitions.boundary_generalization: finite pairwise inequivalent equal-trace peaking states, partitioned into prescribed matrix blocks

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 297 (A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem.; papers: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/297.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Every pure state admits a decreasing net of positive contractions of state value one, strongly decreasing to its minimal support and excising every coefficient; a peaking projection sequence has the same properties, with centered two-index compression tending to zero.
For inequivalent pure states and decreasing excision nets x_lambda,y_nu, norm(x_lambda a y_nu) tends to zero on the full product directed set for every fixed coefficient a.
If B has no finite-dimensional irreducible representations, every tracial state has value zero on the minimal support of every pure state of B.

Strictly trace-decreasing peaking projections with trace tending to zero generate a convergent-sequence algebra admitting the trace-preserving expectation with finite-atom normalized trace values and pure-state evaluation at infinity.

The reduced amalgamated free-product Hilbert D-module has faithful factor representations, faithful trace-preserving expectations onto D and F, and the dense centered-word spanning description used in the bridge.

For any normed unital ring, an element p with norm(1-p)<=1 and an element w with (1-p)w(1-p)=0 satisfy the stated two-ended norm bound for all d,e. Bounded endpoint families whose d*p and p*e norms tend to zero give norm(d*w*e) tending to zero on the product filter.

For every arbitrary old pure state outside a matching peaking class the corresponding endpoint expectation norm tends to zero; for its designated representative the same holds when the endpoint coefficient has pure-state value zero. Uniformity follows from compactness and monotonicity of the unsquared excision net.

Matrix-unit peak transfer removes at most the two outer G letters. If a core remains, each transferred endpoint has a centered original internal coefficient. Empty cores give either cross-excision, centered projection excision, or the explicitly retained double-matched one-letter boundary term.

Under exactly the hypotheses and representative convention of bridge.tex, equation bridge-word-decay holds for every finite m>=1, every b_j in {s,s*}, every F coefficient with centered internal coefficients, and every pair in bridge-tests, in operator norm on the product of the two excision index sets.
Under the staged bridge hypotheses, every old pure state has exactly one state extension to H(A); its extension is pure.
Under the staged bridge hypotheses, unique extensions of old pure states are equivalent if and only if the old states were equivalent or their old classes are exactly the designated two classes.

For any finite family of pairwise inequivalent equal-trace peaking pure states in A, and any partition into matrix blocks, let F=M_N(A), D be the diagonal sum of the peaking algebras, G the block sum of matrix algebras over their common convergent-sequence algebra, and Z=F*_D G. There is a UCP boundary symbol beta:Z->direct_sum M_block(C) with norm(Q_n z Q_t-J_max(n,t)(beta(z))) tending to zero on N x N for every z and at every fixed matrix amplification. beta(a)=diag(phi_i(a)); on a centered normal form a0 e_uv a1 it has only entry (u,v)=phi_u(a0)phi_v(a1), and it vanishes on normal forms with at least two G letters. Every old pure state extends uniquely and exactly the prescribed blocks of old classes merge.

The staged Lemma na:countable-determination asserts that every pure state on X_delta is the unique state extension of its pure restriction to A[S] for some countable dependency-closed S.
The staged Corollary na:state-count asserts at most continuum many pure states when the iteration ordinal has cardinality at most the continuum.

claims.natural_statement: For any normed unital ring, an element p with norm(1-p)<=1 and an element w with (1-p)w(1-p)=0 satisfy the stated two-ended norm bound for all d,e. Bounded endpoint families whose d*p and p*e norms tend to zero give norm(d*w*e) tending to zero on the product filter.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open Filter

namespace SelectiveBridge

theorem twoEndedIdentity {R : Type*} [Ring R] (p w d e : R)
    (hw : (1 - p) * w * (1 - p) = 0) :
    d * w * e = d * p * w * e + d * (1 - p) * w * p * e := by
  calc
    d * w * e =
        d * p * w * e + d * (1 - p) * w * p * e +
          d * ((1 - p) * w * (1 - p)) * e := by noncomm_ring
    _ = d * p * w * e + d * (1 - p) * w * p * e := by rw [hw]; simp

theorem twoEndedBound {R : Type*} [NormedRing R] (p w d e : R)
    (hp : ‖1 - p‖ ≤ 1) (hw : (1 - p) * w * (1 - p) = 0) :
    ‖d * w * e‖ ≤
      ‖d * p‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖e‖ + ‖d‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e‖ := by
  have hd : ‖d * (1 - p)‖ ≤ ‖d‖ := by
    calc
      ‖d * (1 - p)‖ ≤ ‖d‖ * ‖1 - p‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖d‖ * 1 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hp (norm_nonneg _)
      _ = ‖d‖ := mul_one _
  have hleft : ‖d * p * w * e‖ ≤ ‖d * p‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖e‖ := by
    calc
      ‖d * p * w * e‖ ≤ ‖d * p * w‖ * ‖e‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ (‖d * p‖ * ‖w‖) * ‖e‖ := by
        gcongr
        exact norm_mul_le _ _
  have hright : ‖d * (1 - p) * w * p * e‖ ≤ ‖d‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e‖ := by
    calc
      ‖d * (1 - p) * w * p * e‖ =
          ‖(d * (1 - p) * w) * (p * e)‖ := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ ≤ ‖d * (1 - p) * w‖ * ‖p * e‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ (‖d * (1 - p)‖ * ‖w‖) * ‖p * e‖ := by
        gcongr
        exact norm_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ (‖d‖ * ‖w‖) * ‖p * e‖ := by gcongr
  rw [twoEndedIdentity p w d e hw]
  exact (norm_add_le _ _).trans (add_le_add hleft hright)

theorem productDecay {R X Y : Type*} [NormedRing R]
    (left : Filter X) (right : Filter Y) (p w : R)
    (d : X → R) (e : Y → R) (M N : ℝ)
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hN : 0 ≤ N)
    (hdBound : ∀ i, ‖d i‖ ≤ M) (heBound : ∀ j, ‖e j‖ ≤ N)
    (hp : ‖1 - p‖ ≤ 1) (hw : (1 - p) * w * (1 - p) = 0)
    (hd : Tendsto (fun i => ‖d i * p‖) left (nhds 0))
    (he : Tendsto (fun j => ‖p * e j‖) right (nhds 0)) :
    Tendsto (fun q : X × Y => ‖d q.1 * w * e q.2‖)
      (left.prod right) (nhds 0) := by
  have hdl : Tendsto (fun q : X × Y => ‖d q.1 * p‖)
      (left.prod right) (nhds 0) := hd.comp tendsto_fst
  have her : Tendsto (fun q : X × Y => ‖p * e q.2‖)
      (left.prod right) (nhds 0) := he.comp tendsto_snd
  have hbound : ∀ q : X × Y, ‖d q.1 * w * e q.2‖ ≤
      ‖d q.1 * p‖ * ‖w‖ * N + M * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e q.2‖ := by
    intro q
    calc
      ‖d q.1 * w * e q.2‖ ≤
          ‖d q.1 * p‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖e q.2‖ +
            ‖d q.1‖ * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e q.2‖ :=
        twoEndedBound p w (d q.1) (e q.2) hp hw
      _ ≤ ‖d q.1 * p‖ * ‖w‖ * N + M * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e q.2‖ := by
        gcongr
        · exact heBound q.2
        · exact hdBound q.1
  have hzero : Tendsto
      (fun q : X × Y =>
        ‖d q.1 * p‖ * ‖w‖ * N + M * ‖w‖ * ‖p * e q.2‖)
      (left.prod right) (nhds 0) := by
    simpa using ((hdl.mul_const ‖w‖).mul_const N).add
      (her.const_mul (M * ‖w‖))
  exact squeeze_zero (fun _ => norm_nonneg _) hbound hzero

theorem minProductTendsto :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℕ × ℕ => min q.1 q.2)
      ((atTop : Filter ℕ).prod atTop) atTop := by
  refine tendsto_atTop.2 ?_
  intro n
  have hl : ∀ᶠ q : ℕ × ℕ in (atTop : Filter ℕ).prod atTop, n ≤ q.1 :=
    tendsto_fst.eventually (eventually_ge_atTop n)
  have hr : ∀ᶠ q : ℕ × ℕ in (atTop : Filter ℕ).prod atTop, n ≤ q.2 :=
    tendsto_snd.eventually (eventually_ge_atTop n)
  filter_upwards [hl, hr] with q hq hq'
  exact le_min hq hq'

theorem rectangularMinDecay (g : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hg : Tendsto g atTop (nhds 0)) :
    Tendsto (fun q : ℕ × ℕ => g (min q.1 q.2))
      ((atTop : Filter ℕ).prod atTop) (nhds 0) :=
  hg.comp minProductTendsto

theorem transferCases (m transfers : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (ht : transfers ≤ 2) :
    transfers < m ∨
      (m = 1 ∧ transfers = 1) ∨
      (m = 1 ∧ transfers = 2) ∨
      (m = 2 ∧ transfers = 2) := by
  omega

theorem longCoreRemains (m transfers : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (ht : transfers ≤ 2) :
    1 ≤ m - transfers := by
  omega

end SelectiveBridge

claims.natural_statement: Every pure state admits a decreasing net of positive contractions of state value one, strongly decreasing to its minimal support and excising every coefficient; a peaking projection sequence has the same properties, with centered two-index compression tending to zero.

external_assumptions.source: Kadison, Irreducible operator algebras, PNAS 43 (1957), 273-276; primary scanned article located.

retired_assumptions.reason: Report section 2.1 proves the exact unital decreasing and projection-excision forms used here from Kadison transitivity and the hereditary-kernel construction; the published AAP proposition is provenance, not an undischarged black box.

claims.natural_statement: For inequivalent pure states and decreasing excision nets x_lambda,y_nu, norm(x_lambda a y_nu) tends to zero on the full product directed set for every fixed coefficient a.

retired_assumptions.reason: Report section 2.2 proves the rectangular two-index estimate directly by fixing the right index first and then using excision; it does not assume the cited cross-excision conclusion.

claims.natural_statement: The reduced amalgamated free-product Hilbert D-module has faithful factor representations, faithful trace-preserving expectations onto D and F, and the dense centered-word spanning description used in the bridge.

retired_assumptions.reason: Report section 3 explicitly constructs the required tracial module, factor representations, expectations and faithful trace. No general compatible-embedding theorem is used in this mission.

The bridge is defined by the exact matrix free-product model in the staged source; report section 6 proves the corner and named-unitary identifications directly. Ueda is prior-art provenance, not an assumed identification.

claims.natural_statement: A decreasing net of nonnegative continuous functions on a compact space, with pointwise limit zero, converges uniformly to zero. The finite-open-cover proof in report section 3 discharges this directly; Naimpally-Peters Theorem 1.5 page 306 was also checked in the primary PDF.

The staged Lemma na:peaking-restriction asserts that a projection sequence peaking on a larger algebra also peaks on a smaller unital algebra containing it, and its state has a unique extension to the larger algebra.
The staged Lemma na:unique-chain asserts that property (U) and equivalence of uniquely lifted pure states pass through every continuous chain of unital inclusions.
The staged Lemma na:inequivalent-limit asserts that pure states with inequivalent pure restrictions on a tail of a continuous chain remain inequivalent at its limit.

The staged Corollary na:hnn-restriction asserts that reduced HNN adjunction restricts to any unital base subalgebra containing both data algebras, with restricted expectations and the same stable unitary.

The staged Lemma na:hnn-limit asserts that for fixed compatible data and faithful traces, the closure of an increasing union of reduced HNN adjunctions is the adjunction of the closure of the bases, without a cofinality restriction.

The staged Lemma na:base-peak asserts that the CAR base is separable, simple and faithfully tracial, its standard peaking projections have trace 2^(-n), and every containing unital algebra has no finite-dimensional irreducible representations.

The staged construction uses countable determination and separable pure-state homogeneity to supply a new peaking sequence with trace 2^(-n), peaking to the selected old state on the entire current algebra.

The staged construction asserts that for kappa the successor of the continuum, there is an injective schedule sigma:kappa x kappa->kappa with sigma(beta,eta)>=beta and every countable support below kappa is bounded.

routes.retired_because: A nonzero finite-dimensional C*-algebra has finite-dimensional irreducible representations and therefore violates a bridge hypothesis. Finite truncations can check exact subidentities but cannot settle the universal infinite-dimensional bridge.

Squaring is not operator monotone: the retained exact Jacobian certificate gives 0<=Y<=X<=1 but det(X^2-Y^2)=-1/256. The valid argument uses the decreasing unsquared net and x^2<=x, exactly as the staged source does.

Unrestricted one-letter norm decay is false even for the infinite CAR base with the all-zero and all-one peaks: P_n^2 s P_t^1=s P_max(n,t)^1 has norm one for all n,t. The sharp theorem retains this boundary term; the manuscript excludes its endpoint pair.
